title: The Uncharted Current
premise: Jonah Ravensworth has spent six years hopping closed rail lines across the coast, carrying a surveyor's map of routes that officially don't exist and a debt she can't outrun. When an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave her late father's notes called 'the tollgate,' a salvage expedition hires her as guide — and inside they find a wrecked mail car full of evidence that the railway deliberately buried a disaster, along with her father's name on the manifest. As the expedition's backer moves to silence the find and the tide schedule closes the cave for a season, Jonah must choose between the loyalty she owes her crew and the truth her father died carrying. She brings everyone home alive by sacrificing the map, then publishes the truth under her father's name, finally letting herself stop moving.
about_author: C. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former coastal surveyor who spent a decade mapping tide-dependent access routes along the Pacific Northwest. They write adventure fiction about people whose professions keep them one step ahead of the water.

chapters.title: The Last Scheduled Stop
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She rides a decommissioned spur into a dying port town to sell passage on a 'ghost line' to the salvage crew of the Meridian. We learn she never stays more than three nights anywhere. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a fear that stillness is where the past catches up.

chapters.title: Low Water, High Price
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The expedition's backer, Aldous Vey, offers triple pay for a guide to a cave that only opens at a once-in-a-decade tide. Her father's handwriting on the old survey chart makes her say yes. Emotional beat: temptation — the money could buy her freedom, or so she tells herself.

chapters.title: The Tollgate
chapters.summary: Alternating Jonah and dive-lead Mara Okonkwo's POV. The team enters the cave at slack tide and finds a 1950s mail car wedged deep in the rock, sealed and intact. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as they realize the wreck was never 'lost' — it was hidden.

chapters.title: Manifest
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Among the recovered documents is a shipping ledger proving the railway knowingly ran a failing trestle, and her father's signature on the cover-up order — as witness, not culprit. Emotional beat: grief reframed; the man she mourned was silenced, not disgraced.

chapters.title: What Vey Already Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers Vey's expedition was never salvage — he was sent to destroy the evidence, and the crew are expendable witnesses. She hesitates to tell Jonah, torn between loyalty to her employer and the team. Emotional beat: complicity; the first betrayal that isn't quite a betrayal.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The tide returns early — a storm swell — and the cave entrance closes with two divers still inside. The team improvises an ascent through a flooded chimney using rail-survey equipment. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; Jonah's map knowledge saves lives but costs her the only exit record.

chapters.title: Three Nights in Port
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Trapped in town by the storm and Vey's men watching the rail yard, Jonah does what she swore never to do: she stays put, and the past arrives — Vey reveals her father worked for him. Emotional beat: the cost of stopping; she must decide who her loyalty protects.

chapters.title: The Split
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara gives Jonah Vey's orders to burn the documents and frames the plan: split the evidence, fake its destruction, and get the crew out on the last ghost line. One crew member, Finch, refuses and threatens to sell them out. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth, with a traitor in the dark.

chapters.title: The Ghost Line Runs
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, climax. The escape train races the storm and Vey's pursuit down a line scheduled for demolition that night. Jonah chooses to stop the train at the trestle her father died near, confronting Vey with the ledger as the bridge comes down behind them. Emotional beat: she stops running — on her own terms, at the exact place her story began.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, resolution. Months later, the truth publishes under her father's byline, the map is surrendered to the inquiry, and Mara's crew is cleared. Jonah takes a permanent post maintaining a working coastal line. Emotional beat: resolution — memory honored, truth paid for, and stillness finally chosen instead of feared.
